posts.title: Backwards Into the Future
posts.description: Photo: Rene Huemer Phish is a band that has never looked backwards. The Vermont quartet has eschewed nostalgia for forward motion for the entirety of their forty-plus year career. Thus, when rumors emerged of a run of throwback shows at Madison Square Garden celebrating the years of the mid-‘90s, it felt…strange. Though many bands of their age spend their modern tours looking back at the heydays of their careers by playing songs that were popular decades ago, Phish has consistently churned out new music and made their mark by pushing forward despite their well-loved legacy. Employing set lists typical of their formative years, the first three nights of their nostalgic jaunt contained some notable highlights, though were delivered with varying degrees of success. Their 1993 show popped considerably more than ’92 or ’94, but the entire concept felt a bit contrived. This was not how Phish did business. posts.title: Back Where it All Began
posts.description: 12.31.23 (Andrea Nusinov) As a rhombus rose from the hallowed stage at Madison Square Garden, in one of the most surreal moments in Phish history, an ineffable energy engulfed the room. Whispering from the stage, the fairy tale melody of “The Man Who Stepped into Yesterday” tickled the synapses of all in attendance, and, collectively, the audience realized what they were witnessing. Simultaneously, a long-dormant part of each individual awakened; a visceral energy infused with awe, disbelief and joy was birthed from the hearts of all. Yet these words are inadequate; it was something deeper. Each of us was brought back to our earliest days of falling in love with a band that we could hardly believe existed. A palpable enchantment arose as a concert transformed into an improbable lifetime event for which so many had longed through their decades of unconditional devotion. posts.title: Holy Blankenstein: Spirituality in Sci-Fi Soldier
posts.description: (Johnny Dombrowski) Phish has made a career out of one-upping themselves time and time over, and with Sci-Fi Solidier, they just did it again. To close a mind-bending fall tour, the band performed their most ambitious, multi-faceted and outright brilliant Halloween set of their lives. Sci-Fi Soldier is a work of utter genius—a profound piece of spiritual philosophy wrapped in the band’s irresistible humor and drool-worthy grooves—that delivers on multiple levels and represents the greatest piece of concept-driven art that the Vermont quartet has ever laid down. The cohesive, set-long suite simultaneously hits as shock value comedy, science fiction adventure, and spiritual Truth. Though this work of art can be met on multiple levels of enjoyment, it can only be wholly appreciated when understood in its deepest intention.
